answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent reviewers confirm fraud. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not create free influence: every account needs its own locked capital, and coordinated false reviews risk losing it. A prism of randomized reviewers can reduce collusion, while yarrow and forge serve as memorable names for the stake and audit stages, not substitutes for them. The attacker pays an upfront capital cost and risks forfeiting it.
